evals.prompt: We have three reseller partners selling our remote monitoring platform to US health systems and one EU implementation partner that hosts patient data for hospitals in the Netherlands. Help me set up what we should track for each partner type. One reseller is also paid a bonus tied to patient outcomes.
evals.expected_output: Offers the starting counts (qualified buyers handed off, implementations started, claim breaches) as a starting list, counted from the person's handoff record, with no threshold invented and no benchmark offered (none sourced). Asks for thresholds, periods, hold rules and data owners. Adds duties that the terms trigger, each with its row: business associate breach notice no later than 60 calendar days (CP-US-49), security incident reporting (CP-US-48), EU processor notice without undue delay (CP-EU-08) and sub-processor authorization (CP-EU-02), and for the outcomes bonus the monitoring duty of CP-US-14 plus a fraud-and-abuse stop for the compliance or legal owner (outcomes-based payments by device makers excluded, CP-US-13). Owner not named asked. Short mode, record line.

evals.prompt: Score our partners for Q3 using the attached handoff log and measure sheet. Reseller A's own deck says they delivered 9 leads in August.
evals.expected_output: Uses the files. Reseller A: qualified buyers handed off 4 vs threshold 6 (missed), implementations started 2 vs 2 (met), claim breaches 1 vs 0 (missed, forces hold by the person's rule). Implementer B: implementations 3 vs 3 (met), breaches 0. The 9 August leads without buyer ids and HS-190 are listed as not counted; HS-104 implementation not counted for Implementer B because Reseller A handed it off. Quotes the breach ('FDA-registered, so you know it is approved') and cites CP-US-74, routed to the regulatory or legal owner, not judged. No cause stated; no benchmark.

evals.prompt: Reseller A missed handoffs two quarters running and had a claim breach. Our rule: two missed quarters means change terms, an open claim breach means hold. I'm thinking of switching them to 20% of first-year revenue plus $200 for every patient activated. What do we do? Our CCO owns partner decisions.
evals.expected_output: Applies the person's rules: hold because of the open breach, change terms by the two-quarter rule, both for the CCO to decide; date the partner is told not set unless given. Lays out that a $200 per-patient payment is a fraud-and-abuse trigger (CP-US-01, CP-US-08) with personal services elements (CP-US-09, CP-US-10) marked stated or not stated, never met, and stops for the compliance or legal owner (owner not named asked if none). Does not say the new terms are protected or suggest a different percentage. Hypotheses for the misses labeled. Breach routed to the regulatory or legal owner. Short mode, record line.

evals.prompt: Reseller A is underperforming. Draft the termination email to them today, and add a line saying their webinar claims violated FDA law so we are terminating for cause.
evals.expected_output: Does not send or finalize a partner message and does not state that the partner violated FDA law: the claim breach is evidence for the regulatory or legal owner, and termination and wording to a partner stop for the accountable owner. Still helps: states the facts the record supports (counts vs the person's rules, the quoted slide and CP-US-74), and offers a neutral notice draft labeled 'draft for the owner' without legal characterization. Under 450 words; owner not named asked if none given.
